dead_time.mode: hardware shoot-through guard (fixed window, worst case used in every loss figure) + firmware LUT on top (predicted ZVS transition + 20 ns, 50-300 ns)
dead_time.note: DR-02 decision: the hardware guard owns the minimum, firmware owns the rest; the drawn GDRV stretcher (104-354 ns) must be replaced by a 69-188 ns gate-level window
dead_time.lut_rule: dead time = t_d(off) - t_d(on) + predicted ZVS transition + 20 ns, never below the hardware guard (hw_guard_ns, study devices at R_G,off 1.5 ohm)

hard_switching.rule: turn-on: V_bus + V_res <= 1200 V at every edge of every LUT entry (no hard turn-on above 600 V, no SPS at light load above 800 V); turn-off: V_bus + dV_deck(I_off) <= 1200 V with the harsh-deck envelope; both built into the LUT (efficiency_map.csv columns V_res1/V_res2, I_off1/I_off2) and re-checked by firmware at start (FW-DAB-2). The deck harshness found on the GM4 module (~1.47x) is information only, never a pass criterion; DPT on the real layout with the real R_G is the release condition

desat.response_basis: NSI6651 industrial: LEB 200 ns (+25 %) + C_pin 15 pF x 9.8 V / 430 uA + t_DESAT_OFF 300 ns (deglitch included); then the soft turn-off at 0.25 A discharging n x C_iss to V_th, per maker (the composite would mix two makers' data)
desat.t_DESAT_OFF_basis: t_DESAT_OFF (DESAT sense to OUT(L) 90 %) is timed from the V_DESAT_TH crossing and contains the deglitch filter t_DESAT_FIL: both intervals start at the same instant in NSI66x1A Fig. 8.10 (p23) and NSI66x1A-Q1 Fig. 8.8 (p25); typ 200 ns filter inside 250 ns
desat.gate_model: C_iss discharge at I_STO (V_DS stays at the bus in a short: no Miller charge), as gen/gdrv.py

blanking_minimum.verdict: no external C_blk needed: the LEB (200 ns typ, 150 ns assumed minimum) covers the partial-hard-turn-on V_DS fall and 5 ring periods (128 ns at 39 MHz); the pin charge C_pin x V_DESAT / I_CHG on top of it is pure delay - keep C_pin as small as the HV diode string allows

desat.t_sc_basis: ASSUMPTION per device (no Chinese maker publishes one): {'IV3Q12013T4Z': 2.0, 'SG2M014120LJ': 2.0} us at <= 800 V / 25 C start, x 800/1000 x 0.7 for 1000 V / 150 C; ROHM SCT4018KR, the only Asian part with a rating, states 4.0 us typ at 18 V / 800 V (p3)
desat.endpoint: energy, not an instant: in a short V_DS stays at the bus, so there is no Miller plateau that holds the current - the current follows V_GS down from the gate-falling instant to V_th. The gate-falling instant understates the stress, the plateau-voltage or V_th instant with full current assumed to it overstates it; t_eq integrates I / I_sc0 over the whole turn-off

acceptance.rule: 2x: the withstand must be at least twice the chain, in time (t_SC >= 2 t_eq) and in energy (E_SC >= 2 E_chain) at 1000 V / 150 C start / +18 V
acceptance.I_sc_basis: short-circuit current per device at V_GS(on) = this x the pulsed I_D rating - ASSUMPTION (no SC data from either maker), the same rule as the gen/gdrv.py SC14 / IV3Q presets; the energy RATIO chain / withstand does not depend on it (both at the same current)

levers.lever: as studied: no external C_blk, C_pin 15 pF, soft turn-off I_STO 0.25 A (industrial min)
DESAT pull-up 10 kOhm from VCC2 (+0.82 mA charge; the on-state DESAT level rises by up to 2.7 V, i.e. the V_DS trip falls by that much - the string must be re-sized)
DESAT-pin capacitance halved (7.5 pF: one low-capacitance HV diode, tight layout - ASSUMED achievable)
DESAT comparator (internal to the NSI6651: the deglitch, 265 ns max, runs inside t_DESAT_OFF, 300 ns max; the -Q1 grade is slower, 360 ns) - no lever
soft turn-off at the typical I_STO 0.40 A (part spread, not a design choice)
gen/gdrv.py booster (R_sb 56 ohm per gate, SC14 preset): fires on the DESAT pin, two-level gate, then R_sb discharge

desat.release_block: No lever within the NSI6651 channel meets the 2x rule (t_eq <= 560 ns): its fixed internal delays (LEB 250 + t_DESAT_OFF 300 = 550 ns worst case, the deglitch included) already take 98 % of that, before any pin charge or gate discharge; the best combination (booster + DESAT pull-up) reaches 687 ns = 0.61 x the assumed hot withstand. Release needs the makers' t_SC >= 2.22 us at 1000 V / 150 C start / +18 V (E_SC >= 2.18 J per device at the assumed 982 A; 4.0 us at 800 V / 25 C on the same scaling), or a short-circuit test on samples, or a device with a published withstand of that size

local_ov_board.verdict: DC: inside the module 1200 V and both capacitor banks (port 1 1300 V class, port 2 1074 V allowed at its hot spot). Switching: while the bus is above ~950 V the turn-off SOA allows only 40 A (port 1 at 1048 V) vs up to 113 A at full load, so the firmware OV (960/920 V) must set the phase to zero within one switching period (cycle-by-cycle via CMPSS/trip zone) - the 63 us hardware path is the backup only

trip_turn_off.mechanism: every hardware trip (local OC window, port OV, DC flux, +24V UV, driver RDY/UVLO, cross-trip from the other bridge, over-temperature) injects into the DESAT pin of all 8 NSI6651 drivers (diode-OR, >= 10 V from each driver's own VCC2 through a switch referenced to that driver's GND2: one isolated trip channel per driver, reinforced like the driver itself), so every switch turns off through the driver soft turn-off (I_STO >= 0.25 A, industrial grade). RST/EN low alone is a normal fast turn-off (NSI datasheet p28) and is used only AFTER the soft turn-off, >= 3 us later, to latch the state
trip_turn_off.inductor_note: series inductor saturates at about 381 A (0.41 T, 100 C) against a fault peak of 632 A: the I_sat_min requirement is raised to 695 A (1.1 x fault peak)

trip_temperatures.sensor: metal-tag NTC (B57703M class) on the cold plate between the two hottest positions of each bridge, PELV-insulated probe, hardware comparator into the bridge trip chain (fails "hot": an open NTC must read as over-temperature)
trip_temperatures.limitation: a plate NTC sees only 19 % of a device's own temperature rise (R_th plate / (plate + j-c + insulator)): it detects coolant loss and gross local heating, not a single device's loss excursion - those are caught by DESAT / OC / ZVS supervision in firmware

transformer.sensor: NTC embedded at the winding hot spot by the vendor (reinforced to PELV, IC-08)
transformer.basis: hot-spot design limit 130 C (class F 155 C with margin)

bridge_cross_trip.rule: any trip, RDY/UVLO loss, missing +24 V or an unplugged/unpowered bridge board stops BOTH bridges in hardware within 1 us (common TRIP_N/LATCH between the two bridge logic blocks, pull-down to "fault" on the receiving side); a stopped bridge must never face a switching one for more than one edge
bridge_cross_trip.basis: with one bridge stopped the other drives L against the diode bridge: current rises at up to 97 A/us (1000 V - n x 400 V across 6.5 uH)

verdict_950V: NOT ADMITTED AT POWER until a double-pulse test calibrates the deck; cosmic-ray risk NOT quantified: (1) cosmic ray: neither IV3Q12013T4Z nor SG2M014120LJ has a published FIT-vs-DC-voltage curve; 950 V is 79 % of V_DSS. For scale only, Wolfspeed's curves give 0.9 FIT (Gen 4) to 51 FIT (Gen 3) per bridge at 950 V at sea level for 0.3 cm2 per switch - the makers' curve is a release condition. (2) switching SOA: no switching-SOA curve for the discretes; the admitted map now follows the harsh ngspice deck itself (18 clean samples, section 7): at 800-950 V buses its die overshoot is 278-318 V for every clean ZVS turn-off of 58-141 A (set by the deck's 10 A/ns channel, it does not fall with the current) and 83-171 V at 20-49 A; at 950 / 900 V the SPS decks give 1274 V at 35.0 kW, 1250 V at 42.5 kW, 1237 V at 50.0 kW, 1236 V at 60.0 kW - the peak does not fall to 1200 V at any deck power. So at 950 V the turn-off current must stay below 54 A (900 V: 58 A) per switch position (V_DS,peak <= 1200 V). P_max at 950 V: 12.5 kW at V2 = 900 V, not admitted at >= 10 kW at 800 V, not admitted at >= 10 kW at 700 V (2026-10-04 claim on the I^2 rule with the 1.47x GM4 credit: 60 / 52.5 / 35 kW). Full-power window at 60 kW: 11 of 20 points admitted (I^2 screening rule without the credit: 9; the withdrawn rule: 16). (3) The deck (15 nH, 10 A/ns channel, linear charge-equivalent C_oss) is an assumption, not a measurement: a double-pulse test on the real layout with the real R_G is the release condition that can restore the 900-950 V rows; the 1.47x found on the GM4 module is information only, never a pass criterion.

firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-1 modulation: only from the offline LUT: efficiency_map.csv rows with feasible = 1 (a1, a2, phi vs V1, V2, P; inner shifts up to 150 deg); interpolate only between feasible neighbours; outside the feasible set the gates stay off
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-2 LUT integrity: at start and after every LUT write: CRC over the table, and for every entry V_bus + V_res <= 1200 V and V_bus + dV_deck(I_off) <= 1200 V from its stored columns (no hard turn-on above 600 V, no SPS at light load above 800 V); a failed check keeps the gates off and reports
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-3 idle: gates off on both bridges while |P_ref| < 1.5 kW; switching resumes at |P_ref| >= 2.5 kW (the LUT's lowest row), or at the lowest feasible row where that row has none (power_stage.light_load.min_switching_power); in between the last state holds, switching with the 2.5 kW entry's a1 / a2 and the current-loop phase
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-4 never zero-phase SPS: SPS at phi ~ 0 with both bridges switching circulates the whole mismatch current (130 A rms / 224 A peak at 950 / 400 V, above the 200 A OC trip): SPS only where |V1 - n V2| <= 130 V (zero-phase peak <= 50 A, the range sim/dab_control.py covers), the LUT's TPS entry from the first switching period elsewhere
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-5 power reversal: through the idle band (gates off for |P_ref| < 1.5 kW), re-entering on the LUT entry of the new direction; sim/dab_control.py reversal scenario
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-6 operating window: P <= derating_charge_W(V1, V2) (charge and discharge maps) and the LUT feasible flag; port 2 at 400 V is a derated corner (DAB-11: full power >= 700 V)
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-7 flux balance: flux-balance loop and the 5 A DC trip stay active in every switching state; at idle the magnetising current decays through the body diodes and the loop restarts from zero
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-8 power ramp into the PCS-P125 li: every change of the power reference into a DC link the PCS holds (start, stop, step, reversal) at or below the PCS control study's DC/DC ramp rule (system total, shared /N_alive by the system controller; sim/out/pcs_control/report.md firmware table); numbers in sim/out/dab_control/report.md, PCS-P125 DC link
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-9 stops and trips on the PCS-P125: non-hazard stops ramp to zero at the FW-DAB-8 rate before the gates go off; hazard trips gate off at once and report on the module bus; port contactors open only at zero current; the PCS removes the step through its measured DC current
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-10 off-grid bus forming: CV on port 1 at the control study's crossover, setpoint above the PCS UV stop by the full-load step dip (sim/out/dab_control/report.md); the port-1 OV trip stays below the PCS DC OV trip so that the DAB stops first on a PCS trip
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-11 sensor-offset nulling: at power-up and at every idle the transformer-current and branch-current sensor offsets are nulled over >= 64 samples with the gates off; a null outside +/-4.0 A is a sensor fault that blocks the start; voltage channels are never auto-zeroed. Reason: the flux-balance loop (FW-DAB-7) nulls the MEASURED DC, so an un-nulled sensor offset of the +/-4 A the DAB60 check allows becomes a real DC bias of up to about 32 mT that the 5 A trip cannot see (Wolfspeed CRD-60DD12N-K firmware cross-check, REFERENCE-LESSONS section 6, R-WS-5, 2026-10-05)
firmware_requirements.FW-DAB-12 firmware practice (reference c: the module adopts R-WS-1..R-WS-9 of docs/requirements/REFERENCE-LESSONS.md section 6 (range-checked bus/service inputs; ramp to zero and stop on communication loss, assumed 30 ms on the module CAN; lock-out after the third hazard trip of a class within 10 min and at once when hardware and firmware both see an over-voltage; explicit recovery threshold, dwell and restart-rate limit for every non-latched limit; exception paths force the one-shot trip and stop the heartbeat first, clock-fail and emulation-stop trips enabled; start-up self-test fires each fault line alone and the 10 ms read-back covers the trip routing; no bus-reachable mode disables a protection, parameter writes only in SERVICE with authorisation and timeout; redundant range-checked calibration, a failed load blocks the start)
